**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stem at the soil line (crown area)
- **Key features**:
  - White cottony mycelium clearly visible on the stem surface
  - Small, dark, spherical structures (sclerotia) embedded in the white mycelial mass
  - Stem is girdled/bleached at the soil line
  - Dead/dried tissue above the infection point
  - Infection is right at the soil-stem interface

**Reasoning:**

The image shows a classic stem-base infection with white fungal mats and small round sclerotia forming at the soil line. This matches **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii) precisely:
- White cottony mycelium radiating from the stem base
- Characteristic spherical sclerotia (mustard-seed sized) visible in the mycelial mass
- Girdling of the stem at the soil line

This distinguishes it from **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, which produces larger (rice-grain sized) grayish-black sclerotia embedded *within* stem tissue rather than on the surface, and from **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**, which lacks discrete sclerotia.
